The Story of Shribhooti the Priest

I bow to Lord Jina, who bestows welfare, worshipped by the gods of heaven, and I tell the story of Shribhooti the priest who fell into a lower birth through theft.

In the beautiful city of Sinhpur, there ruled a king named Sinhsen. His queen was Ramdatta. The king was wise and devoted to dharma, and the queen was clever and managed all affairs well. The royal priest was Shribhooti, a deceitful man who had spread the reputation that he was a great truth-teller. Innocent people trusted him and were cheated many times, yet no one could uncover his fraud.

One day a foreigner named Samudradatt fell into his trap. He was from Padmkhandpur, son of Sumitra and Sumitra. Wishing to travel abroad for trade, he possessed five precious gems. He could think of no trustworthy person in his own city to leave them with, so having heard of Shribhooti's reputation, he came to Sinhpur and entrusted his gems to the priest. Shribhooti agreed to keep them safe, and Samudradatt departed happily for Ratnadvip (the Island of Gems).

There he stayed many days and earned great wealth. But on the return voyage, through the ripening of sinful karma, his ship struck a reef and broke apart. Many drowned. Samudradatt barely survived, clinging to a plank, and somehow reached the shore. He went straight to Shribhooti's house.

The crafty priest recognized him from afar. He whispered to those sitting nearby, "Look, some beggar is coming. He will trouble us for no reason." When Samudradatt approached and asked for his gems, Shribhooti said coldly, "What gems? I know nothing of any gems. You are a stranger to me." Samudradatt was devastated. He pleaded and reminded the priest of their meeting, but Shribhooti denied everything.

At last Samudradatt appealed to the king. The wise King Sinhsen devised a test. He had both men brought before him and separately questioned them about the exact number, colour, and shape of the gems. Samudradatt described them perfectly, while Shribhooti, who had already sold some of the gems and hidden the rest, could give no consistent account. The king ordered a search of the priest's house, and the remaining gems were found. Shribhooti was punished and banished, while Samudradatt's property was restored to him.

This story teaches that deceit and theft, no matter how cleverly concealed, are eventually exposed. A reputation built on lies crumbles the moment truth is tested. Those who betray trust for worldly gain invite ruin upon themselves, both in this life and the next.
